title: Rethinking Multi-View Fusion for Urban Representation Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.31850v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Urban region representation learning encodes heterogeneous urban signals, such as mobility flows, points of interest, and land-use patterns, into unified embeddings for downstream tasks, including check-in prediction, crime forecasting, and service demand estimation. Existing approaches rely on globally shared fusion and joint optimization, implicitly assuming uniform modality importance and naturally balanced multi-objective training. However, urban data is inherently heterogeneous. Our empirical analysis reveals two structural issues: (i) modality utility varies markedly across regions, causing static fusion to overemphasize signals from certain modalities; and (ii) heterogeneous objectives exhibit persistent gradient imbalance, causing representational bias and unstable training. translated_title: 重新思考面向城市表示学习的多视图融合
translated_abstract: 城市区域表示学习将异构的城市信号（如人流移动、兴趣点和土地利用模式）编码为统一的嵌入表示，服务于下游任务，包括签到预测、犯罪预测和服务需求估计。现有方法依赖于全局共享的融合与联合优化，隐式假设各模态重要性相同且多目标训练天然平衡。然而，城市数据本质上是异构的。我们的实证分析揭示了两个结构性问题：（i）模态效用在区域间差异显著，导致静态融合过度强调某些模态的信号；（ii）异构目标之间存在持续的梯度不平衡，造成表示偏差和训练不稳定。我们提出了 PRISM，一个面向自适应多视图学习的自调节框架。PRISM 采用自适应的稀疏 MoE 路由来学习区域特定的视图分配，……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文实证揭示城市多视图融合中模态效用区域差异与多目标梯度不平衡两大结构性问题，并提出自适应稀疏MoE路由的自调节框架PRISM来学习区域特定的视图分配，实现更稳健的城市表示学习。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals two structural issues—region-varying modality utility and persistent gradient imbalance among heterogeneous objectives—and proposes PRISM, a self-adjusting framework that adapts sparse MoE routing to learn region-specific view allocations for adaptive multi-view urban representation learning.
